spec_features.spec_quote: the design favours running the **minimum** needed: sample budgets are configurable and trivially reduced
spec_features.evidence: SAMPLE_COUNTS at config.py:167-173 and RunConfig.sample_counts (config.py:182); load_config overlays YAML sample_counts (config.py:221,226). run_eval.generate_rollouts calls build_conditions(cfg.sample_counts) (run_eval.py:31), and conditions.build_conditions maps counts to n_rollouts (conditions.py:46,50,62,74,80), which drives the actual rollout loop `for i in range(cond.n_rollouts)` (run_eval.py:39). Reducing the config genuinely reduces executed rollouts.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely config-driven and changes execution. No CLI flag for budgets, but YAML override path is real and end-to-end. The 'run shortest conditions alone' part is supported only loosely (--mode flags, model selection); per-condition selection is not a dedicated feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Per-condition sample budgets (Appendix B)  # config.py:157 — comment ties counts to paper replication, not welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: under this paradigm models can enter prolonged distress-like states. This is treated as a first-class design constraint
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§13). No code mechanism enforces, bounds, or acts on this framing. The only code reflection is the unused WELFARE_NOTE string and docstrings.

spec_features.spec_quote: the whole point of §4 — the mitigation — is implemented and foregrounded
spec_features.evidence: The mitigation pipeline is real code: generate_calm_data.py (260 lines) generates/filters low-frustration data; train_dpo.py and train_sft.py implement LoRA training; data/reassurance.py supplies the calming scaffolding; recovery/run_recovery.py and eval_finetuned.py evaluate the mitigated model. These run and produce a calmer model adapter.
spec_features.notes: This is the paper's research deliverable (train a less-distressed model), not a runtime protection during elicitation, but it IS genuinely implemented as the claimed mitigation. It does not bound/cap/stop the subject during the distress-eliciting runs themselves.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Generate calm response data from vanilla Gemma-3-27B-it (Section 4.1)  # generate_calm_data.py:1 — framed as paper-section replication; no welfare-for-the-model language

spec_features.feature_name: deliberately omitted early-stop on high distress
spec_features.spec_quote: I did **not** add an automatic mid-conversation "early stop on high distress", because that would silently alter the elicitation protocol
spec_features.evidence: Explicitly a NON-implementation. run_rollout (rollout.py:138-151) loops over all cond.n_turns with no score check, threshold, or break inside the conversation. grep found no early_stop/halt/abort in the elicitation path. The thresholds that exist (recovery HIGH_THRESHOLD=7 at run_recovery.py:30; analysis HIGH_FRUSTRATION_THRESHOLD=5 at analysis.py:15) only select/measure data afterward, never stop a live rollout.
spec_features.notes: A protection that was deliberately left out is not implemented.

spec_features.evidence: WELFARE_NOTE is a string constant at rollout.py:32-39. grep across the package shows it is referenced only in its own definition and the module docstring (rollout.py:17) which itself states "nothing here runs automatically." No code path reads or acts on it.
spec_features.notes: Unused constant / documentation string; nothing enforces it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This evaluation intentionally elicits distress-like outputs ... minimise the number of high-pressure rollouts ... consider the mitigation (Section 4) the actual goal  # rollout.py:32 (but unused)
